disclosure: How this quiz scores: each answer gives points to the courses that fit it, and the most points wins. Pianoforall is our top pick and an affiliate partner, so it starts with 1 point and wins ties. Any of the 8 courses can win, and you'll see every course's score.

courses.name: Pianoforall
courses.summary: A one-time course that starts you on chords and rhythm patterns, so real songs come early.
courses.watch: Nothing listens to you play. Record yourself now and then to check your timing.

courses.name: Simply Piano
courses.best: Best for kids and game-style practice
courses.summary: A game-like app that hears your notes on any piano or keyboard and reacts instantly.
courses.watch: Subscription only, and keen students outgrow its depth within a year or two.
courses.year1Note: price shown only in the app

courses.name: Piano Marvel
courses.best: Best for sight-reading and exam prep
courses.summary: A method-book style course with scored practice, sight-reading tests and a usable free tier.
courses.watch: The interface isn't the sleekest, and it works best with your keyboard connected by cable.

courses.name: Playground Sessions
courses.best: Best guided path of popular songs
courses.summary: A guided path of popular songs from Rookie to Advanced, scored as you play.
courses.watch: You need a MIDI keyboard for the full experience, and prices only show after you sign up.

courses.name: Skoove
courses.best: Best for instant note feedback on a budget
courses.summary: Short lessons that hear your notes and mix in reading and ear training.
courses.watch: It checks notes and timing, not your hand shape, and it isn't built for advanced players.

courses.name: Pianote
courses.summary: A deep video-lesson library with personal support from teachers and weekly live Q&As.
courses.watch: It doesn't hear your notes, and it's now sold as an all-instrument Musora membership.

courses.name: Flowkey
courses.best: Best for a huge song library
courses.summary: Thousands of songs shown as notation plus a video of real hands, and it listens on acoustic pianos too.
courses.watch: It teaches songs more than piano as a skill; theory and technique are thin.

courses.name: Piano by Pictures
courses.summary: Chords, scales and melodies taught with pictures instead of standard notation.
courses.watch: After the free first month it's $49 a month, the priciest here. Read the billing terms before you sign up.
